title: Clocked Abort Decision from a Probabilistic Attempt
statement: Let $S$ be a finite-state deterministic machine, $A$ a finite-state nondeterministic machine, $L$ a language of Boolean words, and $m,T_S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $S$ computes the all-true word of length $m(|x|)$ on every input $x$ within $T_S(|x|)$ steps, and $n\le m(n)$ for every $n$. Suppose also that for every $x,u,v$, if $|u|=m(|x|)$ and the attempt by $A$ on $x$ with witness $u$ halts with a single output bit $v$, then $v$ equals the Boolean indicator of whether $x\in L$; and, for every $x$, a uniformly random Boolean word $u$ of length $m(|x|)$ yields that correct bit with probability at least $1/2$. Then the clocked host machine built from $S$ and $A$ with its looping option disabled decides $L$ within $T_S(n)+m(n)+2+(m(n)+1)$ steps: it halts on every witness, never outputs the incorrect bit, and outputs the correct bit with probability at least $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a finite-state deterministic Boolean machine
$A$ is a finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machine
$L$ is a language of Boolean words
$m,T_S$ are functions from natural numbers to natural numbers
